meta.description: Query and download GEO data, inspect SuperSeries structure, choose processed versus raw paths, and link GEO to SRA.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: The source labels submitter-normalized matrices as trust-dependent, defaults to raw when appropriate, and makes no clinical claim.

practice_boundaries.detail: This is data-access engineering and does not interpret patient outcomes or give diagnostic advice.

methodological_ground.detail: Fresh live GEO/Entrez/FTP retrieval, SuperSeries relations, SRA links, and matrix parsing were exercised against current records.

code_usability.detail: All shipped Python examples and geo_series.py routes completed in an isolated private runtime. The optional R GEOquery reference could not be run because no Rscript executable is present in that private runtime; this is recorded explicitly and deducted, not treated as a Python failure.

functional_suitability.note: GEO search, relations, series matrix, GEO-to-SRA, PubMed links, GEOparse/GEOquery choice, and legacy routes are actionable.

reliability.note: The current geo_series selftest protects the Windows encoding regression and source parsers use explicit UTF-8 replacement handling.

performance_context.note: Relation parsing stops before platform/sample tables and the Skill distinguishes matrices from raw/SRA routes.

agent_usability.note: SuperSeries, processed-vs-raw, GDS, GEOmetadb, and ArrayExpress decision boundaries are clear.

human_usability.note: Failure modes map common GEO mistakes to concrete recovery paths.

security.note: No credentials are embedded; Entrez email placeholders are visible and no arbitrary code path was found.

maintainability.note: Runnable scripts are separated from references; R-side execution remains environment-dependent.

agent_specific.note: The source gives strong escape hatches for raw SRA, local re-normalization, and legacy resources; the R parity path could not be exercised here.

key_strengths: All current Python examples, GEOparse, relation streaming, matrix parsing, PubMed links, and both GEO-to-SRA routes completed in an agent-private environment.
The encoding selftest and real matrix parses substantiate the explicit UTF-8 handling required on Windows.
The source protects against SuperSeries, processing-trust, and raw-read workflow mistakes with concrete decision paths.

recommendations.title: Re-run GEOquery parity in a dedicated R runtime
recommendations.problem: The private audit runtime has no Rscript executable, so the optional GEOquery reference was not live-verified.
recommendations.root_cause: Audit-runtime capability gap, not a Python source failure.
recommendations.fix: Provision a separate R/Bioconductor GEOquery runtime for a later parity check; do not mutate shared database-lane environments.
